macMatch.offsetNote: “MAC difference ±N” compares MACs as numbers (same OUI): for routers/ONUs whose MACs differ by a few counts, e.g. ONU …50 and router …51, including across octet boundaries. The nearest ONU is chosen; ties or one ONU claimed by two sessions are flagged ambiguous. “-N octets” only matches the MAC prefix.
macMatch.summary: {{sessions}} active sessions · {{onus}} non-ZTE ONUs scanned · {{match}} match
macMatch.note: Only non-ZTE ONUs with an empty name (NA) are scanned. Apply writes the PPPoE username to the ONU Name and PPPoE fields. Ambiguous matches (several ONUs sharing a MAC prefix — usually the same vendor OUI) cannot be selected; reduce the octet strip or set the name manually.

flow.setupDesc: See where customer traffic on this router goes: Google, YouTube, Meta, TikTok, Netflix and more, with charts and top customers. Data comes from MikroTik Traffic Flow; the NMS only receives data and never changes the router. Each device has its own view.
flow.disabledNote: Not enabled. Press Enable, then run the command below on the MikroTik.
flow.waiting: Waiting for data from {{name}} ({{ip}}) on UDP port {{port}}. Make sure the command was run on this MikroTik and the server firewall allows the port.
flow.cmdHint: Replace interfaces=all with your LAN/customer interfaces if needed. The router must reach the NMS server IP.
flow.noChart: Not enough data for the chart yet. It fills in after a few minutes.
flow.unresolvedHint: {{pct}}% of traffic has no recognised service yet. Names are learned from the router DNS cache and reverse DNS, so this improves over time. Customers using other DNS (e.g. 8.8.8.8) are harder to identify.
flow.noClients: No customer data for this range yet.
flow.senderIpHint: Leave empty if the router sends from {{ip}} (this device's IP). Fill it in if the router sends from another IP, e.g. a loopback address.
flow.noteTitle: How to read these numbers (sampling notes)
flow.noteSource: Source: MikroTik Traffic Flow (NetFlow/IPFIX). The NMS only receives flow reports (connection + byte counts); packet contents are never read.
flow.noteAccuracy: The NMS does no sampling of its own: every received flow is counted. Numbers can run slightly low if UDP packets are lost. Set the MikroTik active-flow-timeout to about 1 minute so long connections (streaming) are reported regularly.
flow.noteBucket: Data is summarised per 5 minutes (1–24 h charts) and per hour (7 and 30 days) and written to the database every 60 seconds, so charts can lag by about 1 minute.
flow.noteClients: Customers with very little traffic (under 20 KB) are held back until they reach a useful size, so they may not appear in the list immediately.
flow.noteDirection: Download/upload is decided from the local networks in settings. If a customer IP is outside that list, direction may be wrong.
flow.noteService: Service names come from the router DNS cache, reverse DNS and domain rules. Unrecognised traffic goes to "Other"; services behind shared CDNs may be less accurate.
flow.noteRetention: Retention: 5-minute data 3 days, hourly data 60 days, per-customer data 7 days (configurable).
flow.noteUse: Good for trends and comparing services. Do not use it for exact billing or quota.
